sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the accounts view
sections.what: Brings in the icons, the account and state types, the window component and the general filter setting.
sections.why: Needed by the accounts view and the logo.

sections.name: AccountLogo
sections.title: Account logo with fallback
sections.what: Shows the company's logo image, or a building icon if there is no logo or the image fails to load. Once an image fails, the icon stays for that account.
sections.why: Keeps the account list looking complete even when logos are missing.
sections.watch_out: The logo file is named after the account id, so an id with unusual characters must be encoded correctly, which the code does.

sections.name: Accounts (part 1)
sections.title: Client tabs, search and research button
sections.what: Draws the row of client logo tabs, a search box, and a top bar that says how many sourced signals match the current choice. The owner can pick all signals, the general market, or one client, and can queue research for the chosen client. The research button is disabled while research is pending, for the general market, or for a client with no web domain.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the owner focus the signal feed on one client without leaving the page.
sections.watch_out: A client with no domain cannot be researched, and the disabled button gives little explanation beyond the status line.

sections.name: Accounts (part 2)
sections.title: Empty search message in client directory
sections.what: Shows a short message inside the client directory popup when the search matches no client.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops the popup from looking broken when a search finds nothing.

summary: Part of the opportunity map accounts view. The part shown here draws a company logo, or a building icon when the logo is missing or fails to load.
purpose: Shows a recognizable logo for each opportunity account in the accounts list.
why: Likely reason: a logo image is nicer to scan than text alone, and the building icon is a fallback. Reason not stated in the code.
how: `AccountLogo` checks whether the account has a logo address. If it does not, it shows the building icon. If it does, it loads a PNG from the opportunity-logos folder, named by the account id. If that image fails to load, it switches to the building icon for the rest of the session of that component.
inputs: One `OpportunityAccount` record, which must include an id and optionally a logo flag.
outputs: A picture or a building icon. Nothing is saved or sent anywhere.
risks: Only the first 13 lines and the first two of four sections are visible, so the rest of the file, including the accounts list itself, is not explained here. The logo path is built from the account id, so a changed id breaks the logo.
debug: If logos are missing, check the file name in the opportunity-logos folder against the account id, and check that the logo flag is set. The browser's network tab will show the failed image request.
